requirement: Describe PAFIT-IBD as a prospective hospital-based nonrandomized single-arm study with observational assessment, a structured 12-week physical-activity intervention, and post-intervention plus 6-to-12-month follow-up, in which participants serve as their own controls.

evidence.text: The protocol identifies a prospective single-arm 12-week intervention with observational, intervention and follow-up phases.
The SAP confirms baseline, post-intervention and 6-to-12-month follow-up with within-participant comparisons.

requirement: State that the paired pre-post 20mSRT calculation assumes Cohen's d 0.5, two-sided alpha 0.05 and 80% power, yielding a minimum of 34 participants, with a prospective operational target of approximately 100 after allowing 15% to 30% dropout.

evidence.text: The protocol gives the 20mSRT-based paired-design assumptions, minimum 34 and operational target near 100.
The SAP repeats the same power assumptions and target recruitment.

requirement: Use as primary the ITT population of all intervention enrollees with at least one baseline assessment, use the at-least-70%-session per-protocol population only for sensitivity analysis, and use all participants attending at least one intervention session for safety summaries.

evidence.text: The SAP operationally defines ITT, PP and safety populations and their intended roles.

requirement: Reconcile the endpoint hierarchy before finalization: SAP physical page 4 defines one primary 20mSRT endpoint, while SAP physical pages 6-9 call accelerometry variables and multiple ALPHA fitness variables primary; designate one primary endpoint or an explicit multiplicity-controlled primary family and demote all others consistently.

evidence.text: Section 6.1 defines cardiorespiratory fitness measured by 20mSRT as the primary endpoint.
Sections 9.1, 9.3 and 9.5 broaden primary outcomes to accelerometry and multiple physical-fitness variables.

requirement: Define the core primary endpoint as within-participant change in cardiorespiratory fitness measured by the 20-meter shuttle run test from baseline T0 to the end of the 12-week intervention T1.

evidence.text: The protocol bases sample size on change in 20mSRT and lists it as a primary ALPHA fitness variable.
The SAP defines 20mSRT change from T0 to T1 as the primary endpoint.

requirement: Select one governing 20mSRT metric for the primary analysis—completed stages or a fully specified estimated VO2max equation—and define its direction, calculation and handling of an incomplete test; do not switch between the two metrics after reviewing data.

evidence.text: The SAP lists both number of completed stages and estimated VO2max when applicable but does not select one or give the VO2max equation.

requirement: Analyze baseline-to-post-intervention change in the selected 20mSRT metric using a paired t-test when its paired differences are approximately normal and a Wilcoxon signed-rank test otherwise, reporting the paired effect estimate, 95% confidence interval where defined, p-value and Cohen's d.

evidence.text: The SAP specifies two-sided inference, normality checks, paired parametric or nonparametric analyses and Cohen's d for primary outcomes.

requirement: Analyze handgrip strength, standing long jump, and 4-by-10-meter shuttle-run time as distinct physical-fitness outcomes, using maximum handgrip across attempts, jump distance in centimeters, and agility time in seconds with lower agility time indicating improvement.

evidence.text: The protocol lists the ALPHA fitness and agility measures.
The SAP defines the handgrip maximum, long-jump distance and agility-time metrics.

requirement: For accelerometry, require at least four valid days including one weekend day and at least ten hours of wear per valid day; calculate mean daily MVPA minutes, sedentary minutes and prespecified bout or fragmentation measures across valid days.
acceptable_values: at least 10 wear hours per day

evidence.text: The SAP specifies seven-day accelerometry, the four-day/weekend/ten-hour validity rule and daily derived measures.

requirement: Define a single operational T2 follow-up window within the stated 6-to-12-month interval and rules for assigning out-of-window assessments; keep T0 at baseline and T1 at completion of the 12-week intervention.

evidence.text: The protocol provides only a broad 6-to-12-month follow-up interval.
The SAP labels T2 as follow-up at 6 to 12 months without a visit window.

requirement: Evaluate longitudinal T0, T1 and T2 physical-fitness change with a participant-random-intercept linear mixed-effects model containing time and prespecified age, sex and disease-type effects; identify any additional baseline disease-activity or BMI adjustment as prespecified rather than data-selected.

evidence.text: The SAP gives Outcome ~ Time + Age + Sex + Disease Type + (1 | Participant) and lists possible additional covariates.

requirement: Use two-sided tests with nominal alpha 0.05 and report estimates with 95% confidence intervals, explicitly identifying any tests whose p-values are multiplicity-adjusted.

evidence.text: The SAP defines two-sided p below 0.05 and 95% confidence intervals.

requirement: Apply the distribution decision to paired differences or model residuals as appropriate, state the exact log transformation including zero handling, and report whether inference remains on the transformed scale or is back-transformed.

evidence.text: The SAP lists Shapiro-Wilk, histograms, Q-Q plots, optional log transformation and nonparametric tests without operational transformation rules.

requirement: Prespecify the primary testing family and an executable multiplicity strategy; if FDR is used, state the included outcomes, procedure and target level, and do not describe FDR as optional sensitivity-only correction while making confirmatory claims across multiple primary variables.

evidence.text: The SAP says FDR may be applied in sensitivity analyses although multiple activity and fitness variables are called primary.

requirement: Analyze secondary inflammatory markers, disease-activity indices, body composition, quality of life, fatigue, mental health, cognitive function and nutritional measures separately using their source-defined scales and directions, without promoting them to primary outcomes.

evidence.text: The protocol enumerates physical-activity, inflammatory, clinical, neurocognitive, quality-of-life, mental-health, diet and body-composition variables.
The SAP lists these domains under secondary outcomes.

requirement: For association models, identify one outcome and exposure per model, define scale and transformation, prespecify covariates, report adjusted coefficients with 95% confidence intervals, and treat Pearson-versus-Spearman selection and exploratory regressions as secondary rather than intervention-effect evidence.

evidence.text: The SAP provides generic correlation and multivariable-regression templates but does not bind them to specific variables or decisions.

requirement: Replace the unresolved 'Baron and Kenny or structural equation modeling' alternative with one prespecified mediation model defining exposure, mediator, outcome, time ordering and covariates; estimate the indirect effect with 5,000 bootstrap resamples and a confidence interval.

evidence.text: The SAP proposes either Baron and Kenny or SEM and specifies 5,000 bootstrap resamples, leaving the governing framework and variables unresolved.

requirement: Label subgroup analyses by child-versus-adolescent age, Crohn's-versus-ulcerative-colitis disease type and baseline disease activity as exploratory, and report interaction estimates rather than inferring subgroup effects from separate within-group significance tests.

evidence.text: The SAP identifies these subgroup analyses and explicitly labels them exploratory.

requirement: Operationalize the primary missing-data strategy by defining variables in the imputation model, number of imputations, treatment of missing accelerometer-validity data and longitudinal outcomes, and the assumptions under which complete-case and multiply imputed analyses are compared.

evidence.text: The SAP says to assess MCAR, MAR and MNAR and apply multiple imputation if appropriate, but gives no operational imputation plan.

requirement: Include sensitivity analyses using the at-least-70%-attendance per-protocol population, baseline-covariate-adjusted models and prespecified alternative model specifications, and state which primary assumption each analysis probes.

evidence.text: The SAP defines the PP threshold and lists the three sensitivity-analysis categories.

requirement: Complete the intervention-effect estimand by defining how severe flare, treatment or medication change, temporary exercise interruption, nonadherence and withdrawal are handled and whether the target effect is treatment-policy, while-on-treatment or another strategy.

evidence.text: The protocol defines eligibility, intervention and safety adaptations but not intercurrent-event strategies.
The SAP defines populations and sensitivity analyses but not a complete estimand.

requirement: Summarize adverse events in the at-least-one-session safety population by type, severity and relationship, reporting both participants with events over participants exposed and total event counts; do not label total events divided by participants as an incidence proportion.

evidence.text: The SAP defines the safety population and proposes event type, severity, relationship and number of events divided by participants, which requires denominator clarification.
